result.topic_en: The page finishes worked examples of making $xy(xx-yy)$ equal to a given number α times a square, then gives Fragment 39 (Lexell): a method for solving $\alpha xx+\beta yy=\gamma zz$ from a known solution $\alpha ff+\beta gg=\gamma hh$ by factoring with imaginary square roots.
result.transcription:
Fragmenta ex Adversariis deprompta. 205
III. Si $\alpha=23$, sumatur $x=156^2$ et $y=133^2$, erit $xy(xx-yy)=23.\,156^2.\,133^2.\,289.\,42025$.
IV. Ut $\alpha=41$, capiatur $x=21^2$ et $y=20^2$, erit $xy(xx-yy)=41.\,21^2.\,20^2.\,29^2$.
V. Ut fiat $\alpha=31$, sumatur $x=40^2$ et $y=9^2$, fit enim
$xy(xx-yy)=31.\,9^2.\,40^2.\,7^2.\,41^2$.
VI. In genere si capiatur $x=4ppqq$ et $y=(pp-qq)^2$, fiet
$xy(xx-yy)=(pp-qq+2pq)(2pq-pp+qq).\Box$.
Unde si sit $2pq+pp-qq=aa$, fit $\alpha=2pq-pp+qq$, at illa formula $2pq+pp-qq$ fit quadratum sumendo $q=2rs$ et $p=2rr+ss-2rs$.
VII. Deinde vero si sumatur $x=(2pp+qq)^2$ et $y=(2pp-qq)^2$, fiet
$xy(xx-yy)=8pp.qq(8p^4+2q^4)\Box=(4p^4+q^4)\Box$
unde fit $\alpha\Box=4p^4+q^4=(2pp+2pq+qq)(2pp-2pq+qq)$.
Unde si fuerit $2pp+2pq+qq=\Box$, tunc erit $\alpha=2pp-2pq+qq$. At illud evenit
si $p=2rs$ et $q=rr-ss-2rs$, unde fit $\alpha=pp+(p-q)^2$.
VIII. Ex casu VII, si $p=5$ et $q=7$, capiatur $x=99^2$ et $y=1$, erit $\alpha=29$ et $xy(xx-yy)=29\Box$;
vel si capiatur $x=29.13^2$ et $y=70^2$.
A. m. T. I. p. 21. 22.
39.
(Lexell.)
Problema. Invenire numeros $x$, $y$, $z$, ut fiat $\alpha xx+\beta yy=\gamma zz$, siquidem cognitus fuerit casus
$\alpha ff+\beta gg=\gamma hh$.
Solutio. Statuatur $\alpha xx+\beta yy=(\alpha ff+\beta gg)(\alpha pp+\beta qq)^2$, tum enim erit
$\alpha xx+\beta yy=\gamma hh(\alpha pp+\beta qq)^2$, sicque erit $z=h(\alpha pp+\beta qq)$;
illud autem hoc modo per factores praestetur. Sit $x\sqrt{\alpha}+y\sqrt{-\beta}=(f\sqrt{\alpha}+g\sqrt{-\beta})(p\sqrt{\alpha}+q\sqrt{-\beta})^2$, tum enim sponte fit $x\sqrt{\alpha}-y\sqrt{-\beta}=(f\sqrt{\alpha}-g\sqrt{-\beta})(p\sqrt{\alpha}-q\sqrt{-\beta})^2$, quarum formularum productum ipsa est aequatio supposita. Prior autem evoluta dat
$x\sqrt{\alpha}+y\sqrt{-\beta}=\alpha fpp\sqrt{\alpha}-\beta fqq\sqrt{\alpha}\mp 2\beta gpq\sqrt{\alpha}$
$+\alpha gpp\sqrt{-\beta}-\beta gqq\sqrt{-\beta}+2\alpha fpq\sqrt{-\beta}$
$x=f(\alpha pp-\beta qq)-2\beta gpq$
$y=g(\alpha pp-\beta qq)+2\alpha fpq$
ac tum erit $z=h(\alpha pp+\beta qq)$.
Verum haec solutio nondum est generalis, eodem modo enim ponere potuissemus
$\alpha xx+\beta yy=(\alpha ff+\beta gg)(pp+\alpha\beta qq)^2$,
unde fit $z=h(pp+\alpha\beta qq)$. Pro hoc ergo casu statuatur
$x\sqrt{\alpha}+y\sqrt{-\beta}=(f\sqrt{\alpha}+g\sqrt{-\beta})(p+q\sqrt{-\alpha\beta})^2$,
cujus evolutio praebet
$x=f(pp-\alpha\beta qq)-2g\beta pq$
$y=g(pp-\alpha\beta qq)+2f\alpha pq$.
Verum ne hi ambo quidem casus solutionem praebent generalem, cum sine dubio ejusmodi casus dentur, quibus $z$ non per $h$ fit divisibile, quare pro solutione generali statuatur
$\alpha xx+\beta yy=(\alpha ff+\beta gg)(\alpha npp+\beta nqq)^2$, unde fit $z=hn(\alpha pp+\beta qq)$,
ubi forte $n$ potest esse fractio denominatoris $h$. Statuatur igitur
$x\sqrt{\alpha}+y\sqrt{-\beta}=(f\sqrt{\alpha}+g\sqrt{-\beta})(p\sqrt{\alpha n}+q\sqrt{-\beta n})^2$,
cujus evolutio praebet

items.quote:
Problema. Invenire numeros $x$, $y$, $z$, ut fiat $\alpha xx+\beta yy=\gamma zz$, siquidem cognitus fuerit casus
$\alpha ff+\beta gg=\gamma hh$.
items.english: Problem. To find numbers x, y, z such that αxx+βyy=γzz, given that a case αff+βgg=γhh is known.

items.quote: Verum haec solutio nondum est generalis
items.english: But this solution is not yet general.

items.quote: Verum ne hi ambo quidem casus solutionem praebent generalem, cum sine dubio ejusmodi casus dentur, quibus $z$ non per $h$ fit divisibile
items.english: But not even both these cases give the general solution, since without doubt there are cases in which z is not divisible by h.

items.quote: ubi forte $n$ potest esse fractio denominatoris $h$
items.english: where perhaps n can be a fraction with denominator h.
